title: How do we break a tenth and then a unit?
description: Two lengths in units, tenths and hundredths are taken from each other by breaking a tenth and then a unit. The breaking is compared with taking two hundred sixty eight from six hundred fifty three. Keeko takes the smaller number from the bigger one in every place.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the top number in a place is too small, break one from the next bigger place, one place at a time. Watch for students who subtract the smaller number from the bigger one in each place.

source: Find 15 3/10 4/100 - 2 6/10 8/100, and compare the steps with 653 - 268.
video_script.why: The child has broken one tenth into hundredths and now breaks a tenth and then a unit in the same take away.
video_script.substitution: Where the top number is too small, break one from the next bigger place, and do this one place at a time.
video_script.anchor: Two lengths, 15 3/10 4/100 and 2 6/10 8/100, written in columns of units, tenths and hundredths
video_script.wrong_answer: thirteen and three tenths and four hundredths
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the smaller number from the bigger one in each place, 6 - 3, 8 - 4 and 15 - 2, instead of taking the lower number from the upper one.
video_script.payoff_line: The answer is twelve units, six tenths, and six hundredths

final_answer.spoken: twelve units, six tenths, and six hundredths

never_show: the smaller number taken from the bigger number in a place
maths_rules: Hundredths: 4 is less than 8, so break 1 tenth: 15 3/10 4/100 = 15 2/10 14/100.
Tenths: 2 is less than 6, so break 1 unit into 10 tenths: 15 2/10 14/100 = 14 12/10 14/100.
653 - 268: the ones are too few, so a ten breaks into ones; then the tens are too few, so a hundred breaks into tens. 653 - 268 = 385.
Slip: the lower number is taken from the upper number, never the smaller from the bigger.
video_script.design: One idea: break a tenth, then a unit, one place at a time. Assumes the child can break one tenth into ten hundredths. Wrong idea: take the smaller number from the bigger one in each place. The columns stay on the board and the comparison with whole numbers comes last.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two lengths are written in units, tenths, and hundredths, and one is taken from the other.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we find the difference, and how does it compare with taking away whole numbers?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one unit block breaks into ten tenth blocks; one tenth block breaks into ten hundredth blocks

marks.unit: one unit block breaks into ten tenth blocks
marks.tenth: one tenth block breaks into ten hundredth blocks

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>One unit breaks into ten tenths, and one tenth breaks into ten hundredths.
<bookmark mark='tenth'/>We break only when a place has too few to take away from.

marks.given: the two lengths are written in columns

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, fifteen units, three tenths, and four hundredths. Take away two units, six tenths, and eight hundredths.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the difference of the two lengths.

beats.on_screen: Hundredths: 4 is less than 8, so break 1 tenth: 15 3/10 4/100 = 15 2/10 14/100

marks.one: the hundredths column glows, 4 is less than 8
marks.break: one tenth breaks into 10 hundredths, giving 15 2/10 14/100

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, look at the hundredths. Four is less than eight, so break one tenth.
<bookmark mark='break'/>Three tenths becomes two tenths, and the hundredths become fourteen.

beats.on_screen: Tenths: 2 is less than 6, so break 1 unit: 15 2/10 14/100 = 14 12/10 14/100

marks.two: the tenths column glows, 2 is less than 6
marks.break: one unit breaks into 10 tenths, giving 14 12/10 14/100

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, look at the tenths. Two is less than six, so break one unit into ten tenths.
<bookmark mark='break'/>Fifteen units becomes fourteen units, and the tenths become twelve.

marks.three: 14 - 8 = 6 is written under the hundredths column
marks.rest: 12 - 6 = 6 and 14 - 2 = 12 are written under the tenths and units columns

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, subtract place by place. Fourteen take away eight leaves six hundredths.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Twelve take away six leaves six tenths, and fourteen take away two leaves twelve units.

beats.on_screen: 653 - 268: ones too few, a ten breaks into ones; then tens too few, a hundred breaks into tens

marks.same: arrows show a ten breaking into ones and a hundred breaking into tens

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, compare with six hundred fifty three take away two hundred sixty eight. The ones are too few, so a ten breaks into ones.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Then the tens are too few, so a hundred breaks into tens. It is the same breaking, one place at a time.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The answer is twelve units, six tenths, and six hundredths.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko says thirteen and three tenths and four hundredths. Keeko took the smaller number from the bigger one in every place.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But we take the lower number from the upper number. When the upper number is too small, we break from the next place.
